# Goban Studio v8.0.0

v8 is about doing less, better: a straight road from the first lesson to
the first game, teaching that says why, an opponent that feels right at
the end of a game, a quieter interface, and many bugs fixed.

## Download and first launch

<!-- first-launch -->
| Platform | File | First launch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `GobanStudio-macOS-arm64.dmg` or `.zip` | See the package README. |
| macOS (Intel) | `GobanStudio-macOS-x64.dmg` or `.zip` | See the package README. |
| Windows (x64) | `GobanStudio-Windows-x64.zip` | See the package README. |
<!-- /first-launch -->

`SHA256SUMS` lists the checksums of every file. Windows on ARM runs the x64
build under the system's emulation. v7 can update itself to v8 from
Settings → About.

## From the first lesson to the first game

- **Capture Go.** After the lesson on capturing, the lesson's last page
  offers a game of capture Go on 9×9: whoever captures first wins. It needs
  only what you just learned — no counting, no dead stones. The computer is
  gentle at first and a little stronger once you have won twice. Capture Go
  games are not rated, saved or analysed, and the offer goes away once you
  have won two.
- **Your first 9×9 game.** After the lessons on eyes and living groups, the
  lesson page offers your first real game: 9×9 against the gentlest
  computer level, with teaching mode on.
- **"I know the rules"** at the first launch now starts a 9×9 game
  (about ten minutes) instead of 19×19.
- **The first count** explains itself once, in three sentences: how the
  game ends, what dead stones are (tap a group to change it), and what the
  score and komi mean.

## Teaching that says why

- When teaching mode warns about a costly move, it now says why in one
  line: "This move may cost about 16 points — your group at B8 can no
  longer make two eyes", "White can catch your stones in a ladder",
  "White can capture it at once".
- A hint names its reason too: "Consider D5 — it cuts White apart".
- The reasons come from the same reading as the review and the report, so
  the three agree. When the app is not sure of a reason, it gives none.
- **The course was checked by KataGo** on GitHub's build machines: every
  "place" step (107) and every board in a "read" step (51). Where KataGo
  clearly disagreed, the lesson was corrected — the finished 9×9 game used
  in the counting lessons (its walls had cutting points, and the count was
  wrong), two game-order steps, a whole-board judgement diagram and a joseki
  step. `docs/lesson-audit.md` lists every change and every disagreement
  left for a human to judge.

## Playing feel

- **"Shall we count?"** now appears reliably on your turn once the board is
  settled; before, the computer's own move often cleared it at once. After
  "Keep playing" it waits a few moves before asking again.
- **Resigning** waits until the computer is behind by more than what is
  still open on the board, not just 15 points with much of the board
  unsettled. Undo no longer lets an earlier hopeless streak trigger an
  instant resignation. The gentlest levels still play every game out.
- **Dead stones** are judged group by group: a group is never half dead,
  stones in seki live, and a stone left in atari at the end is dead. Your
  corrections are no longer overwritten while the judgement is being made.
- **The computer's move comes first**: background analysis now pauses the
  moment the computer has to move, then carries on.
- **13×13 measured** for the first time (960 games): the strength estimate
  now uses 13×13 measurements, and the suggested 13×13 human-style opponent
  is one level gentler for players around 25 and 15 kyu.

## Quieter

- The play panel says one quiet line before the first move.
- The review keeps its status — the analysis and where the game left the
  opening book — on one line.
- Today offers one thing to learn: the Daily five, then the next lesson.
- Library has three tabs: the pro-opening drills now live with the
  explorer, under Openings.
- Reports of your games are made by themselves in the background; there is
  no "Analyse all" button and no list of background work to manage.
- Settings has five panes; the opponents' networks close the Playing pane.
- Importing problem collections is a quiet link at the foot of Practice
  until you have one.
- Faster start: the opening book loads when it is first needed (the app
  script is 20 % smaller, first paint about 100 ms sooner).

## Fixes

- Trying a move in "Review so far" no longer plays it in your game.
- Imported problems that are due now take part in the Daily five's reviews.
- Drills made while reviewing classic games no longer count as your weak
  points in the training plan.
- An SGF whose first move is in its root node keeps that move; a handicap
  record without komi is read with the handicap komi (0.5), not 6.5.
- A game saved during the count can be finished after restarting.
- "Guess the next move" works from a game's last move.
- The Daily five skips a drill that no longer exists.
- A broken streak no longer shows on Today; the streak no longer resets on
  the day clocks change.
- The Won and Lost filters no longer count a draw as lost.
- Editing an old game's comment no longer counts it as played this week or
  moves it to the top of the Library.
- When storage is full, saving says so instead of "Saved".
- Cancelling an update download and starting it again shows "Restart to
  update" again.
- Going back to a finished lesson no longer fails.
- Reports from before v7 that no longer fit their (since edited) game are
  made again.

## Known limits

- The builds are not code-signed (no certificates yet). The update
  checksum guards against damaged or wrong downloads; it is not a
  signature.
- Not yet checked by people: a usability test, a strong player's review of
  the course and the explorer, a native-speaker review of the Chinese,
  Korean and Japanese text, and a real screen-reader session.
- The KataGo check of the course leaves some steps for a human: rule steps,
  small shape boards where KataGo prefers a big point elsewhere, the
  endgame boards whose open areas make an invasion best, and one 3-3
  joseki step where KataGo prefers a cut to the standard connection.
- 13×13 handicap games were not measured (about 2.5 ranks a stone, as
  before). The standard ladder and its 10-kyu anchor were not measured
  again.
- The desktop app can pick many problem files at once but not a whole
  folder. Wide-open problems (for example ladders) usually cannot be proved
  and are not imported.
- The counting solver ignores ko threats; endgame problems avoid ko.

## Your data

Everything from v7 carries over.
